care_continuity: National isolation/CTE stock: 819. The source prints no complete national capacity denominator.
Ituri: 484 patients for 978 beds (49.5%); Nord-Kivu: 262 for 220 beds; Haut-Uele: 68 for 128 beds; Tshopo: 5 for 25 beds (20.0%). Sud-Kivu publishes no isolation block this cut.

Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uele are carried at their DERIVED occupancy (119.1% and 53.1%) because the printed percentages disagree with the printed patient and bed counts: SR115 prints 123.2% for Nord-Kivu, which corresponds to 271 patients rather than the 262 it also prints, and 50.8% for Haut-Uele, which corresponds to 65 rather than 68 and is the same figure SR114 printed.
Bas-Uele reports no CTE/CT and no ambulance and publishes no occupancy block; its values remain unset rather than inferred.
The four reporting provinces sum to 819 exactly, matching the printed national stock with no unallocated residual.
challenges: Alert volume fell 13.6% (1 628 to 1 406) with Sud-Kivu again not reporting, and verification stands at 82.4% (1 159/1 406). Across seven cuts the series has swung +50.2%, -30.3%, +53.1%, -31.3%, +19.6%, -24.1%, -13.6% with no INSP correction to the completeness and time-window question SR109 raised. Treat it as a reporting-coverage artefact, not a transmission signal.

Care capacity: Nord-Kivu is oversaturated for a fourth consecutive cycle, with 262 patients against 220 beds, and some patients are still held in non-normative facilities. In Ituri the Nizi, Mambasa and Mandima sites are saturated for suspects and 39 patients are in critical condition, with extension at Nizi and construction at Bambu still in progress. Bas-Uele still has no CTE/CT and no ambulance.

Contact follow-up eased to 85.3% (20 888/24 479) from the printed 85.7%. Tshopo sits at 59.1% (191/323), Bas-Uele at 70.4% (107/152) and Haut-Uele at 76.1% (900/1 183). Sud-Kivu publishes no contact row. INSP attributes the weakness to insufficient teams dedicated to surveillance and contact follow-up in Bas-Uele, while noting an improvement there.

PoE/PoC operation stays weak: national report completeness 76.2%, with Bas-Uele at 34.6% (9 of 26 expected), Sud-Kivu 55.5% (5/9) and Haut-Uele 64.0% (7/11), where four points (Dusu, Apodo, Aungba, Gossamu) transmitted nothing for lack of internet. Only 9.1% of Ituri's strategic points are functional: Avakubi is down for insecurity, four points (Nzebi, Galay, Pluto, Bey) are on strike over non-payment and two (Chamugamba, Pabiri) are unreachable; Tshopo has activated 18 of 30 planned PoC.

Infection prevention in Ituri remains far short: 15 rings opened of 69 expected (21.7%), and 5 bodies could not be swabbed because of community resistance at Nia-Nia and Mandima. Haut-Uele transmitted no PCI/EDS data at all this cut.

Ervebo remains stocked out at Buta, suspending vaccination of priority personnel, with no mobility for advanced-strategy teams and no vaccination micro-plan in the six priority Bas-Uele zones (Aketi, Ango, Bili, Buta, Ganga, Viadana).

Community resistance persists: in Haut-Uele a confirmed escapee found at Nduka (Isiro) refused to return to the CTE, with her husband threatening suicide and 22 contacts listed along her route; in Tshopo there is resistance to investigation, sampling, isolation and transfer, with 10 contacts refusing follow-up at Matete (Mangobo); in Bas-Uele impassable roads and absent mobile coverage in several villages.
No new health zone was affected. The footprint holds at 61 of 151 health zones across six provinces.

The page-one cumulative sentence dates the totals to 05 September while the edition reports on 06 September; the totals themselves are the 06 September figures, since they close exactly on this cut's movement (6 604 + 82 and 3 175 + 51). The 40.3% footprint truncation seen at SR113 and SR114 does NOT recur: SR115 prints 40.4% throughout.
highlights: Footprint: 61/151 health zones across six provinces; no new zone this cut.
Nord-Kivu is over isolation capacity for a fourth consecutive cut (262 patients, 220 beds).

poe_poc_national.coverage_note: 84.6% report completeness, up from 78.9%; Ituri 87%, Nord-Kivu 100%, Tshopo 94%, Sud-Kivu 55.5%, Haut-Uele 55.0%, Bas-Uele did not report its completeness indicators. Only 9.1% of Ituri's strategic points and 55.0% of Haut-Uele's are functional (31.8% nationally). At Haut-Uele five points (Doko, Dusu, Apodo, Aungba, Gossamu) transmitted nothing for lack of connection; at Tshopo only 18 of 30 planned PoC are activated (60%).

priorities: Answer the completeness and time-window question on the alert series: seven cuts of large unexplained swings now stand uncorrected.

Restore PoE/PoC operation and reporting: Bas-Uele is at 34.6% report completeness, Haut-Uele has four points off the network for lack of internet, Ituri has only 9.1% of strategic points functional with four on strike over non-payment, and Tshopo has activated 18 of 30 planned PoC.

Relieve the Nord-Kivu oversaturation, now a fourth consecutive cycle above capacity at 262 patients against 220 beds, and the saturated Ituri suspect capacity at Nizi, Mambasa and Mandima; Bas-Uele still lacks a CTE/CT and an ambulance.
Close the Ervebo stock-out at Buta and put vaccination micro-plans in place for the six priority Bas-Uele health zones.
Reconcile the two care-capacity percentages that contradict their own printed patient and bed counts (Nord-Kivu 123.2%, Haut-Uele 50.8%).

preserved_conflicts: The full 24-hour death movement is 41: 32 community plus 9 intra-CTE deaths; the cover community count is a subset.
SR115 is DRC-only at 6686 confirmed / 3226 deaths; country scope adds the unchanged Uganda anchor (20/2/11).
The 366 Ituri deaths printed as A ventiler remain an unventilated health-zone residual; the 5 intra-CTE deaths on that row are the Ituri intra-CTE deaths pending allocation, not an additional count.
National isolation stock is a direct printed count; the source does not publish a complete national capacity denominator, which remains null.
Page-one prose prints the 61/151 footprint as 40.3% while the sidebar and Table 1 both print 40.4%; 61/151 = 40.397%, so 40.4% is promoted and the prose cell recorded as a source truncation.

The edition back-references the previous day's contact follow-up as 85.9%, while SR113 printed 86.0%. SR113's own figures (21 909/25 500) compute to 85.92%, so the back-reference is arithmetically correct and SR113's printed value was a rounding error. The released SR113 snapshot is immutable and is not restated.
Tshopo appears twice in the printed zone table, once as a province header and once as a health zone inside its own province; both are retained as printed.

movement_basis: printed 24-hour columns of the edition per-health-zone table; cumulative movement closes on the edition totals
